config.prompt: Duty of care at the boundaries — file each claim:

items.label: foreseeability, proximity, and fair-just-and-reasonable all found
rescuing a drowning stranger — the individualist signature
a builder's negligent delay damaging wallets, not bodies
negligent misstatement — the Hedley Byrne carve-out
psychiatric harm within the defined classes of claimant
secondary victims beyond the controlled thresholds

config.why: Caparo's third limb is where courts decline duties that would crush socially useful risk-taking — the exceptions are a theory of what the tort system is for.

activities.caption: true or false — who actually pays
activities.name: tortCarelessJudge

statements.s: All four elements must be satisfied before anyone pays.
statements.why: A claim that fails at breach never reaches causation.

statements.s: A careful driver who skids on unforeseeable black ice owes nothing.
statements.why: The standard is conduct-relative, not outcome-based.

statements.s: Tort exists to compensate every accident, fault or not.
statements.why: It prices unreasonable risk — the gap is what no-fault systems were invented to close.

statements.s: A foreseeable loss caused by conduct meeting the standard is still somebody's tort.
statements.why: Meeting the standard means no breach — the reasonable person is the measure, not the outcome.

activities.caption: find the line the courtroom drama wrote
activities.name: tortDamagesSpot

config.prompt: One line of this damages summary is drama, not doctrine — click it:
lines: Special damages: quantified pecuniary loss, future loss converted to lump sums via multipliers.
General damages: pain, suffering, loss of amenity — tariffed by judicial guidelines.
Contributory negligence reduces damages by the claimant's percentage share.
Exemplary damages are a routine feature — every serious wrong earns a punishment top-up.
Defendants are almost always insured — tort works as distributed insurance with fault-based gating.
config.correction: English law confines exemplary damages to narrow categories — punishment is the criminal law's department.
config.why: Volenti is narrow in practice, effectively barred in employment and road cases; illegality was recalibrated by Patel v Mirza.

activities.anchor: abnormally sensitive uses get less protection
activities.caption: drag the divider — private, then public
activities.name: tortNuisanceCompare

config.prompt: Two kinds of nuisance — drag the divider:

before.label: Private nuisance
before.text: An occupier's use and enjoyment against unreasonable interference — judged by locality, duration, sensitivity, gravity against utility; the injunction is the default for continuing interference.

after.label: Public nuisance
after.text: Shared rights — obstructing a highway — grounding representative claims.

config.why: Rylands v Fletcher added strict liability: bring something dangerous onto land (reservoir water) and it escapes, you answer without proof of negligence — partially absorbed into negligence and statutory regimes since.

activities.caption: bet on the two libel regimes
activities.name: tortDefamePredict

config.q: A public-figure plaintiff sues over a story whose falsity they cannot prove was known. Where does the claim go further?
choices: England — claimant-friendly history, serious-harm threshold notwithstanding
The United States — actual malice is an easy bar to clear
Nowhere — defamation claims are always criminal, never civil
config.why: US law's actual-malice requirement makes defamation nearly unreachable for public figures, while England's claimant-friendliness once attracted libel tourism — the 2013 reforms and the anti-SLAPP movement answered it.
